segments.script: Some epithelial cells don't just cover surfaces — they have evolved to beat, absorb, sense, secrete, and produce gametes. These are the modified epithelia.
segments.video_prompt: High-speed macro microscopy animation of cilia beating rhythmically on tracheal epithelium surface — a river of mucus flows over them. Title card: 'Modified Epithelium'. Cinematic teal and deep-blue colour scheme.

segments.script: Six types of modified epithelium: Kino-ciliated (9+2 microtubule arrangement, true motile cilia, moves mucus in respiratory tract, ova in fallopian tubes, CSF in neurocoel). Stereo-ciliated (non-motile microvilli, epididymis, sperm maturation). Brush-bordered (microvilli, intestine and PCT, maximise absorption). Neuro-sensory (receptor cells in taste buds, olfactory epithelium, inner ear). Pigmented (melanin, retina, absorbs excess light). Germinal (gamete production, seminiferous tubules, ovary). Glandular classified by ducts: exocrine, endocrine, heterocrine. By consistency: serous, mucous, mixed. By secretion mode: apocrine, merocrine, holocrine. By cell count: unicellular or multicellular. By structure: simple or compound — tubular, alveolar, tubulo-alveolar.
segments.video_prompt: Six icons appear in a vertical list: a waving cilia icon, a brush border absorption icon, a nerve cell receptor icon, a melanin pigment icon, a gamete production icon, and a secretion droplet icon. Each pulses as named. Then a hierarchical decision tree animation builds from 'Glandular Epithelium' through five branching criteria — each branch appears as a neon-lit node. Goblet cell (unicellular, merocrine) and parotid gland (multicellular, serous, compound) shown as leaf examples. Dark navy background, gold node accents.
